audit.why: Difficulty 7/10 TRICKY against a 49.4% win rate over 1571 games is defensible: Viktor's Gravity Field (W) stun and Hextech Ray (E) both outrange Cassiopeia's 700-range Twin Fang, so the early lane is spacing-dependent even though Cassiopeia's sustained damage wins any fight that lasts.

audit.corrected: spikes[1..3] and content mid/late rewritten with Arcane Storm / Hextech Ray and real cooldowns (E 12/11/10/9/8, R 120/100/80).

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Viktor wins by stunning you inside Gravity Field, then chunking you with Hextech Ray from outside fang range.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. It governs your forward steps. - R Petrifying Gaze spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Gravity Field is 17s at rank 1, 13s at rank 5 — the stun only fires if you linger inside, so walk out and step up while it recharges. - Hextech Ray is 12s at rank 1, Siphon Power 9s. - Petrifying Gaze is 120s — spend it on his Arcane Storm channel.

edits.before: Carry by DPS — no mid matches your damage-per-second from two items; your job is staying alive long enough to prove it.
edits.after: Carry by outlasting Viktor's burst: his shield Q and Arcane Storm want short fights, and every second past them belongs to you.

edits.before: Ahead, suffocate: poison every last-hit, zone Viktor off the wave with fang threat, and call your jungler — your W makes every gank a guaranteed kill.
edits.after: Ahead, suffocate: poison every last-hit and push the wave to his tower — Viktor has no dash, so Miasma into Petrifying Gaze makes any jungler who arrives a kill.

edits.before: Q the last-hit window, E-E-E while the poison ticks, and walk back as it fades — three fangs and out, repeat until Viktor is executable.
edits.after: Noxious Blast first — Twin Fang only hits hard on a poisoned target, and at 40 mana on a 0.75s cooldown you can chain three before the poison fades.

edits.before: Viktor spends Gravity Field early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Miasma grounds and slows: drop it behind him and he cannot walk out of your fang range.

edits.before: That’s Viktor’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Hextech Ray outranges your 700 fang — sidestep the line, don't tank it for CS.

edits.before: Spamming unpoisoned fangs at full mana cost, or holding W so long the dash you were saving it for already happened.
edits.after: Unpoisoned Twin Fang costs the same 40 mana for a fraction of the damage — no Blast, no E, or you lose the mana war outright.

edits.before: Track Viktor’s Gravity Field: The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Gravity Field (17s) — the stun only fires if you linger inside, so step out and trade on its downtime. Petrifying Gaze cancels his Arcane Storm channel.

edits.before: Chaos Storm is a strong teamfight tool but doesn't save Viktor in lane — your Petrifying Gaze stuns through his Hex Core shield timing if you catch him without Gravity Field up.
edits.after: Arcane Storm is a channel — your Petrifying Gaze cancels it outright, and a 120-second ultimate thrown away in lane is his worst trade. Step up while Gravity Field is on its 17-second cooldown.

edits.before: Once Viktor gets Hex Core upgrades his poke sharpens, so this phase is his best window to fight back with Death Ray zoning, but your DoT still wins extended trades if he ever misplays position.
edits.after: Once Viktor augments Hextech Ray his wave clear and poke both sharpen, so this is his best window to fight back, but Noxious Blast into fang spam still wins every trade that outlasts his 8-second E.

edits.before: Liandry's or Rabadon's push your damage well past Viktor's burst combo, and your mobility lets you dodge Chaos Storm's follow-up while punishing him with poison stacking in skirmishes.
edits.after: Liandry's or Rabadon's push your damage well past Viktor's burst, and your passive-boosted movement walks you out of Arcane Storm while poison keeps ticking him down through the skirmish.

edits.before: Viktor's Hex Core power spike at levels 4-5 sharpens his poke and makes this the closest part of the lane, so play a bit more patiently and avoid walking into Death Ray angles. Once you're both 6, his Chaos Storm is a teamfight-oriented ultimate rather than a lane-winning tool, and your Petrifying Gaze stun still lets you punish any overextension or missed Gravity Field.
edits.after: Viktor's augment spike at levels 4-5 sharpens his poke and makes this the closest part of the lane, so stay off the line of his Hextech Ray and step in on its 8-second cooldown. Once you're both 6, his Arcane Storm is a channel that your Petrifying Gaze interrupts outright — hold R for that cast rather than a missed Gravity Field, and his ultimate is gone for 100 seconds.

edits.before: Viktor scales into a strong teamfight threat with Chaos Storm zoning, but in a direct lane skirmish your DoT damage and stun outpace his kit as long as you dodge his Gravity Field setup. Build toward Liandry's or burst items and keep applying pressure — his damage ramps slower than your poison ticks in prolonged exchanges.
edits.after: Viktor scales into a real teamfight threat with Arcane Storm zoning, but in a direct skirmish your DoT and Petrifying Gaze outpace him as long as you step out of Gravity Field before it stuns. Build Liandry's into Rabadon's and keep the pressure on — his burst ramps slower than your poison ticks in anything that lasts.

edits.before: Poke with Death Ray once Hex Core upgrades come online
edits.after: Poke with Hextech Ray once his augments come online
